final_message_excerpt:
The investigation is submitted and frozen: 35 findings, all citing evidence. I did not re-read the report text after submitting.

- **Initiating event:** a single-phase-to-earth fault on the Eaton Socon–Wymondley Main 400 kV line began at 16:52:33.490 BST (15:52:33.490 UTC), 4.5 km from Wymondley Main. Protection opened both ends in 70 ms and 74 ms, inside the 80 ms Grid Code figure NGET cites. The circuit was auto-reclosed at 16:52:53, and no defects were found afterwards. Lightning is the accepted cause, but three strikes were recorded at the same second, so the record cannot say which one hit the line.
- **Generation lost:**
  - Hornsea One lost 737 MW at about 16:52:33.7 (799 MW down to 62 MW). Ørsted attributes this to a sub-synchronous control resonance. Why the controllers were insufficiently damped is unresolved.
  - Little Barford lost 641 MW in three steps, ST1C (244 MW) at about 16:52:35, GT1A (210 MW) at about 16:53:30 and GT1B (187 MW) at about 16:53:58. The root causes of the steam-turbine speed-signal discrepancy and the later steam-pressure rise are not established.
  - Embedded generation losses are estimates only, because DNOs hold no real-time data. They include about 500 MW on loss-of-mains protection and a net 200 MW at 49 Hz. A further 550–581 MW was inferred around LFDD operation, and the 100 MW source is unexplained.
  - Total generation lost depends on the basis used. ESO Appendix H gives 1,528 MW initially, and ESO's cumulative table reaches 1,878 MW. Ofgem gives at least 1,990 MW, and E3C interim gives about 2,100 MW.
- **Frequency:** the first minimum was 49.083 Hz at 16:52:59, and the overall minimum was 48.787 Hz at 16:53:49. Frequency was below 49.5 Hz for 142 s, so the 60 s expectation was missed, and below 49.0 Hz for about 33 s. It first reached 50.0 Hz at 16:57:16. All of this comes from 1 s samples, so timings are good to about ±1 s.
- **Containment:** ESO was securing for a 1,000 MW loss with 1,022 MW primary and 1,314 MW seconda
